transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what brings me in is that I keep hearing these... very clear voices. It happens mostly in my apartment, and sometimes when I'm in empty museum rooms. It sounds exactly like women whispering from behind the walls, and they keep telling me which photographs belong in the archive. It's just been happening a lot, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
Do the voices tell you to do anything or influence your actions in any way?

Well, no, not really. They don't give me orders or... or make me do things, if that's what you mean. It's just what I said, them whispering about the photographs and the archive. I don't actually act on it or do anything with the pictures, I just... I just hear them talking.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?
No, I haven't. I mean, my mood has been fine, really. I haven't been feeling sad or down at all... it's just those voices that are the issue.
Do you believe the voices you hear are real?

Yes, I do. I mean, I hear them clearly, so they are real to me. And... well, I am convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone anyway. They know my Caribbean archive will change how the galleries tell the truth. Nobody has shown me anything that proves otherwise, so... yes, I believe it's all very real.
Do you think the museum board and the city arts people are actually against you or trying to harm you in any way?

I don't know if they want to physically hurt me, but... yes, they are definitely against me. Like I just mentioned, I am absolutely convinced the museum board and the city arts people are monitoring my phone. They're doing it because they know what I have. My Caribbean archive is going to completely change how the galleries tell the truth, and they want to keep an eye on me because of that. It's just a fact. No one has shown me a single piece of evidence that proves otherwise, so I know they're listening to my calls.
Do you often find it difficult to keep your thoughts organized or to follow a logical sequence when talking or thinking about something?

Yes, I suppose I do. For example, when my cousin asks me a simple question about a bill or an appointment, I try to answer her. But then I start explaining the grant... and then the shipping routes... and then my grandmother’s altar. By the time I stop talking, nobody seems to know what I meant. So, yes, I guess it can be hard to just follow a straight line when I'm explaining things.
Do you have difficulty completing tasks or achieving your goals due to your thoughts or behaviors?

Yes, I do. Honestly... I've lost the trust of my colleagues over all this. I've missed board meetings, and I just haven't been paying my bills. It got to the point where my cousin and one of the museum administrators actually had to step in. I just... I couldn't manage my appointments or handle my money anymore. They felt I couldn't even navigate public events safely on my own. So, yes, getting things done has become very difficult.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt extremely energetic, happy, or irritable, and didn't need much sleep?

Yes, I do. There are days when I just feel... radiant. Like I've been chosen for this specific purpose, and I have all the energy in the world to get it done. I don't really need to sleep when I feel like that. But then... if someone questions my plan, or if my cousin tells me I need to slow down, I just get furious. It's like they're trying to erase me and the work I'm doing. So, yes, I get very energized, but also very irritable if people get in my way.
Have you ever considered the possibility that the museum board and city arts people might not be monitoring your phone?

No, I haven't. I mean, I am absolutely convinced that they are monitoring my phone. The museum board and the city arts people... they know that my Caribbean archive is going to completely change how the galleries tell the truth. It's too important, and they want to keep an eye on what I'm doing. No one has shown me a single piece of evidence that proves they aren't listening. So, no, I haven't really considered that they aren't.
Do you believe your Caribbean archive will have a significantly greater impact on the world than what most people would expect from such a project?

No, I... I don't think so. I mean, it's an important project for the galleries, like I said, but I don't believe it's going to change the whole world or anything like that. It's just an archive. I'm really just trying to make sure the history is told correctly here. I don't have any... grand expectations beyond that.
Do you feel like you're specially gifted or have a unique role in the world that sets you apart from others?

No, I wouldn't say I'm specially gifted or anything. I mean, earlier I said I felt chosen, but... that's just a feeling I get when I have all that energy. It's not like I actually think I'm better than anyone else or have some grand destiny. I'm just a 64-year-old woman working on a local history project. I don't think I have a unique role in the world, just... just the work I'm doing right now.
Do you think there are other people or organizations, besides the museum board and city arts people, that are against you or trying to harm you?

No, I don't think so. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it's really just the museum board and the city arts people. I don't have any reason to believe anyone else is involved. 

But I am still absolutely convinced that those two groups have been monitoring my phone. It's because they know my Caribbean archive is going to change how the galleries tell the truth around here. And... well, no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise. So, no, just them.
Do you think your Caribbean archive project is the most important thing happening in the world right now?

No, no, I wouldn't say it's the most important thing happening in the world. I mean, there's a lot going on everywhere else. It's just... it's important to me, and it's important for the local history here. But I don't think it's the center of the universe or anything like that. It's just my work.
Have you ever had a period where your elevated mood and energy lasted for several days or more at a time?

Yes, I do. I get these stretches of days where I just feel... radiant. Like I'm chosen, which I guess is what I was trying to explain earlier. 

But it's not just that good feeling. If someone questions my plan during those days, or if they tell me I need to slow down, I become absolutely furious. It feels as if they are trying to erase me. So, yes, those periods definitely last for several days at a time.
Are the thoughts about the museum board and city arts people monitoring your phone something you think about for most of the day?

Yes, I would say it's on my mind for most of the day. It's... it's hard not to think about it when it's happening to you. 

Like I said a few minutes ago, I am just completely convinced that the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. They know exactly what I'm doing. They know my Caribbean archive is going to change how the galleries tell the truth around here, and they want to keep tabs on me. And, well, no one has shown me a single piece of evidence that proves otherwise. So, yes, it takes up a lot of my time and my thoughts.
Do you think your work on the Caribbean archive will make you famous or widely recognized?

No, I don't think it'll make me famous. I don't really care about being famous or... or getting recognized by the whole world. It's just about the work itself, and making sure the truth is out there for the people here. I'm not looking for my name in lights or anything like that.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or energetic that lasted for weeks at a time?

Well, I wouldn't say it's just one long stretch of weeks, but... if I look back over the past year, those bursts where I barely sleep, where my mind is just racing with plans and I'm spending money and just full of this furious energy... they add up. I'd say I've spent about six months out of the year in that state. It just keeps coming back.
Do you think your ideas about the museum board and city arts people monitoring your phone are more prominent when you're feeling extremely energetic or happy?

Well, no, I wouldn't say they only happen then. Actually, there was a period of several weeks where I wasn't feeling especially energized or grand at all. My energy was just... normal, I guess. But even then, I remained completely convinced that the arts people were monitoring my phone. And I still heard whispers in my apartment during that whole time, too. So it doesn't seem to just be tied to when I have all that extra energy.
Are your thoughts about the museum board and city arts people monitoring your phone something that you think about every single day?

Yes, I do think about it every single day. I mean... I am completely convinced that the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. They know my work on the Caribbean archive is going to completely change how the galleries tell the truth, so they're keeping tabs on me. And honestly, no one has shown me a single piece of evidence that proves otherwise, so it's just a fact I have to live with every day.
Do you think your thoughts about the museum board and city arts people monitoring your phone are more intense when you're feeling extremely energetic?

Well, they definitely happen at the same time, yes. When I was in that state—sleeping just a few hours a night, rushing around trying to get all my archive tasks done—I was absolutely certain the board was tracking everything I did. And I was hearing those women's voices whispering, too, right in the middle of all that energy. So, yes, they were very intense then, even though, like I said, they don't completely go away when my energy goes back to normal.
